summary: The milestone completed 4 experiments in 113.7 minutes, including 2 compute-bound experiments. The compute-bound paths took 33.6 and 22.58 minutes, but the supplied evidence does not divide those totals into queueing, model loading, inference, or artifact-writing phases. The locked task-level indicator reports no GPU idle on compute-bound work; the standalone idle snapshot does not establish utilization while those tasks were running.
bottlenecks_identified: The finite-choice channel qualification was the longest compute-bound path at 33.6 minutes; its title indicates broader qualification scope, but the data does not identify which execution phase caused the duration.
The forensic Qwen diagnosis was the other compute-bound path at 22.58 minutes, with no phase-level timing to distinguish model setup, inference, diagnosis, and result serialization.

Disk-mtime reconstruction provides end-to-end ordering but no task-correlated GPU, concurrency, or runner trace, so GPU efficiency and runner selection cannot be causally evaluated from the idle snapshot alone.
improvements_suggested: Emit per-experiment phase timings for queueing, model load, warm-up, inference, evaluation, and artifact writing so the next retrospective can target measured slow phases.
Add a task-correlated GPU engagement probe for compute-bound launches that records device assignment and utilization during the task, while leaving synthesis-only tasks exempt.
Record model count, concurrent-model intent, and selected runner; route through DualGPURunner only when at least 2 models are actually loaded in parallel.
Persist per-model finite-choice qualification receipts so later gated qualification can reuse completed checks when inputs and model hashes are unchanged.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Instrument phase-level timings on every compute-bound experiment.
Correlate GPU utilization samples with experiment start and stop boundaries.
Capture concurrency intent and conditionally select DualGPURunner for confirmed multi-model parallel tasks.
meta_reflection: The bounded evidence ranks the compute-bound work but does not support a causal explanation for its runtime. Because it contains neither a timed counterfactual nor phase-specific loss, the defensible savings estimate is 0.
